meta.description: Tikpal Voice vs Plaud Note: price, included AI minutes, subscriptions, and what each recorder is built for. An honest, factual comparison to help you choose.

hero.title: Looking for a Plaud alternative?
hero.subtitle: Plaud and Tikpal both turn speech into something useful — but they're built around different jobs. Here's the honest comparison.

shared.title: What both do well
points: Record your voice with dedicated hardware instead of a phone.
Use AI to turn speech into text and summaries.
Work with a companion app on iOS and Android.
Built for people who think out loud — founders, creators, professionals.

table.title: Tikpal Voice vs Plaud Note
table.intro: Plaud details reflect public information from plaud.ai and press coverage at the time of writing (early 2026). Check each site for the latest.

rows.label: Beyond the included minutes
rows.tikpal: AI pauses until the next month; recording continues — no paid tier to unlock
rows.plaud: More minutes require a subscription (around $99.96/year for 1,200 minutes)

rows.label: Built around
rows.tikpal: Capture → Remember → Recall → Act: organized memory, tasks, integrations
rows.plaud: Record → Transcribe → Summarize: meeting notes and transcripts

rows.label: Integrations
rows.plaud: Transcription and summaries inside the Plaud app

tikpalPoints: You want spoken thoughts to become memory you can search later — not just transcripts.
You want AI minutes included with the device, with no subscription tier to unlock.
You want ideas routed to Notion, Todoist, Gmail or Calendar in one sentence.
plaudPoints: Most of your recording is meetings and calls, and transcripts plus summaries are the main goal.
You prefer a thin, card-shaped recorder.
You're happy to pay a subscription for higher transcription limits.
